name: Kadindi
body:
KADINDI
CR 13

This enormous ogrish hulk is covered with shaggy black hair. Its mouth hangs open, fangs bared and lit by an inner red glow.

XP 25,600
Unique NE Huge monstrous humanoid (shapechanger)
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft., scent, see invisibility; Perception +21
Aura frightful presence (120 ft., DC 22)

DEFENSE

AC 28, touch 11, flat-footed 25 (+2 Dex, +1 dodge, +17 natural, –2 size)
hp 184 (16d10+96)
Fort +13, Ref +12, Will +12
SR 24
Weaknesses running water aversion

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft.
Melee club +22/+17/+12/+7 (3d6+8) or cage of chains +22/+17/+12/+7 (3d6+8 plus grab), bite +22 (3d6+12)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 15 ft. (10 ft. with bite)
Special Attacks cage of chains, devour, grab (Medium), swallow whole (3d6+12 damage plus 3d6 acid damage, AC 18, 18 hp), roaring inhalation
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 11th; concentration +15)

Constant—see invisibility, speak with animals
At will—beast shape III (animals only)
7/day—magic missile, minor image (DC 16), shield
3/day—dimension door, dispel magic, fear (DC 18), scorching ray
1/day—baleful polymorph (DC 19), dominate person (DC 19)

STATISTICS

Str 27, Dex 15, Con 22, Int 16, Wis 15, Cha 18
Base Atk +16; CMB +26 (+30 grapple); CMD 39
Feats Cleave, Combat Expertise, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Mobility, Power Attack, Spring Attack, Whirlwind Attack
Skills Climb +27, Intimidate +23, Knowledge (arcana) +19, Perception +21, Sense Motive +18, Spellcraft +19, Survival +21
Languages Abyssal, Common, Giant, Infernal; speak with animals

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Cage of Chains (Su)

Kadindi wields a massive flail-like weapon known as the cage of chains. This weapon functions as a Huge flail, but any Medium or smaller creature struck by it is also grabbed, as animated chains in the cage attempt to grapple the creature. The cage of chains uses Kadindi’s CMB and CMD for all grapple-related checks. Kadindi doesn’t gain the grappled condition while holding a creature in the cage and can move freely. However, attacks made with the cage of chains suffer a –2 penalty while a creature is held within. The cage can hold only one creature at a time. At the start of each of Kadindi’s turns, the cage attempts to pin the grappled creature. If successful, it then attempts to tie up the creature. The chains animate only for Kadindi, and cease functioning if he dies.

Devour (Su)

As a standard action, Kadindi can transfer a pinned or tied up creature from the cage of chains to his mouth. The creature is bitten and then swallowed whole. Kadindi must succeed on a grapple combat maneuver to do this against a pinned creature, but automatically succeeds against a tied up creature. Kadindi’s has a tooth-lined gullet that chews on swallowed creatures, dealing bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, similar to a bite attack.

Gaping Maw (Ex)

Kadindi’s jaws can stretch unnaturally wide.

Kadindi always adds 1-1/2 times its Strength bonus to his bite damage even when using bite attacks in combination with manufactured weapons. Kadindi still takes –5 penalty on bite attack rolls when combining attacks like this. When using Cleave with a bite attack, Kadindi can still make an attack roll against the second creature, even if the attack against the first creature misses.

Roaring Inhalation (Su)

As a standard action, Kadindi stretches its jaws wide and inhales with a deafening sucking wind. All Medium or smaller creatures in a 20-foot cone are pulled 15 feet toward Kadindi. Kadindi makes free maneuver checks (CMB +24) to pull these creatures closer. All creatures in the cone must succeed on a DC 24 Fortitude save or be staggered for 1 round. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Running Water Aversion (Ex)

Kadindi cannot cross running water unless magically compelled.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary
Treasure standard (Huge flail, Huge club, other treasure)

The Kadindi, also known as the “Swallower-of-Men” or “Dodo” is Hausa folklore in sub-Saharan West Africa.

Revered as the “King of Beasts,” Kadindi embodies both terror and mystique. Rooted in West African folklore, stories of survivor’s encounters serve as reminders of the delicate balance between nature and humanity, emphasizing respect for the natural world. The cultural significance of Kadindi lies in its role as a witty yet cautionary figure, reminding communities of the importance of generosity and fairness.

Kadindi is a legendary ogre-like creature with shaggy black hair and a glowing red mouth. He is a shapeshifter, capable of taking on forms such as lions, elephants, or pythons, symbolizing his vast dominion over all creatures. Despite a fearsome nature, Kadindi is known to intelligently interact with humans in dialogue, often demanding payment or tribute in exchange for sparing lives.

Kadindi demands offerings of meat, but his hunger is insatiable and no amount is ever enough to placate him. He may invite himself to eat and could even offer a morsel from his own supplies, but in the end those sharing hospitality and even giving all that he asks may find themselves snatched up into a great sack or cage he carries for devouring later.

Kadindi is easily distracted, however, and may wander off in quest of new morsels, giving those trapped by him a brief chance to escape. Kadindi takes captives at times and is fond of using them to produce hideous half-monstrous children.

These affairs are never happy and usually end in Kadindi losing interest and his erstwhile captive leman escaping.
